title: Motorway Lanes & Overtaking
whatItIs: On a motorway the left-hand lane is your normal lane. The other lanes are for overtaking, and you move back once you have passed.
keyFacts: Drive in the left-hand lane unless you are overtaking. Move back to it as soon as it is safe.

keyFacts.text: On motorways with 3 or more lanes, you MUST NOT use the right-hand lane if you are towing a trailer.

keyFacts: Overtake only on the right. Don't move to a lane on your left to overtake.
In queues, if the lane on your left is moving faster, you may keep going in it.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT stop on the hard shoulder, except in an emergency or when told to.

items.title: Left-hand lane
items.text: Your normal driving lane. Return to it after overtaking.

items.title: Middle and right lanes
items.text: For overtaking. Move back left when you have passed.

items.title: Towing a trailer or caravan
items.text: Never the right-hand lane on a motorway with 3 or more lanes.

items.title: Hard shoulder
items.text: For emergencies only, unless signs open it as a lane.

a.label: Overtaking on the left
points: Don't move left to pass someone

b.label: Queue moving faster on the left

onTheTest.question: You are towing a caravan on a three-lane motorway. Which lane must you NOT use?
options: The hard shoulder in an emergency
onTheTest.why: Vehicles towing trailers must not use the right-hand lane of a motorway with three or more lanes.

traps: Once you have overtaken, move back left: don't sit in the middle lane.
Towing on a motorway: 60 mph limit, and never the right-hand lane on 3 or more lanes.
Passing on the left is only OK in queues where your lane is moving faster.
